solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Edith relaxing with sons: they seek pleasure

indicators.note: relaxing suggests loosening up, so the letters of the two names and words are let go and rearranged

explanation.surface: Edith unwinds with her sons, all of them pleasure-seekers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxing' rearranges the letters of EDITH and SONS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure, so its followers are people who seek enjoyment above all.

clue.text: Hope to engage sailors with very good dance at sea

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in, so the word hope holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors
PI is short for pious, crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: Someone hopes sailors will join in a fine shipboard dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to engage' signals the insertion; PI (pious) is crossword shorthand for very good, and RN is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is the lively solo jig traditionally associated with sailors aboard ship.

clue.text: Closely follow pointer, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to tail or shadow someone persistently
a pointer is a breed of hunting hound, so an example of the animal

explanation.walkthrough: 'pointer' looks like an arrow or indicator, but it is a breed of gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to trail someone; as a noun, a pointer is one breed of the animal.

clue.text: No bananas for homeless person

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: Someone without a home has no bananas to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed abode, moving from place to place, has no permanent home.

clue.text: Advertisement from Kentish golf course committee?

parts.note: Sandwich in Kent is home to Royal St George's, a famous championship links
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: An advert apparently issued by the committee running a golf club in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in the county of Kent, England, with a well-known Open Championship golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of hinged placards worn front and back by a person on the street is a form of advertising.

clue.text: Member of extended family keeps walking

definitions.meaning: a spouse's child from an earlier marriage, a relative by remarriage

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as STEPS ON to get the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A child gained by marrying their parent joins a blended household, a relation by remarriage.

clue.text: Black and silver container

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A container coloured black and silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack or pouch is a simple holder for carrying things.

clue.text: Got very upset and stopped working

definitions.meaning: lost control of one's emotions, wept
ceased functioning, as a car or machine does

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both collapsing in tears and a machine failing or packing up.

clue.text: Some big reward got bigger

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sizeable prize increased in value.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb meaning to increase in size, so expanded or enlarged.

clue.text: Battalion having no time for course of therapy

indicators.note: having no means the military unit word goes without the following letter

parts.note: a battalion is a unit of a regiment, used loosely here for the regiment

explanation.surface: A military unit with no time for a medical treatment programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' drops the T from REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed plan of diet, exercise or medication is a set programme of treatment.

clue.text: East European turns to run off with partner

indicators.note: turns says the eastern European pair together is turned round, read right to left

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: An Eastern European resorts to running away with a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses E plus POLE, EPOLE, as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee secretly with a lover, usually in order to marry, is the classic runaway romance.

clue.text: Sat for photo, showing composure? Not I

indicators.note: Not says the following letter is left out of the word for composed

parts.note: poised means calm and self-assured

explanation.surface: Someone sat for a photograph looking calm, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not I' removes the I from POISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding a position for a camera or painter is modelling, keeping still in a set attitude.

clue.text: Sporty type in winter's half-skimpy pullover

indicators.note: half of the word skimpy means only its front three letters are kept

parts.note: a jumper is a British word for a knitted pullover

explanation.surface: A winter athlete wearing a skimpy sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes SKI from SKIMPY; JUMPER is British for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who launches off a ramp on skis is a competitor in a winter sport.

clue.text: Drunk spotted reeling in front of Edward

indicators.note: in front of puts the first piece before the name
reeling, spinning round, says the word for seen is turned backwards

parts.note: spotted means saw
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A drunk was seen staggering ahead of a man called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is slang for very intoxicated, heavily inebriated.

clue.text: Fish: medic eats tons

indicators.note: eats means the doctor word swallows the following letter

parts.note: a surgeon is a medical doctor

explanation.surface: A fish-eating doctor consumes tons of it.
explanation.definitionFit: This large, armoured fish of rivers and seas is the source of caviar.

clue.text: Regal figure organised prison concert

indicators.note: organised suggests putting things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal personage arranged a concert at a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The husband of a reigning queen, like Prince Albert or Prince Philip, is a royal title holder.

clue.text: Sound happy crossing street in English city

indicators.note: crossing means the cheering word straddles the following piece

parts.note: to cheer is to make a happy noise

explanation.surface: Someone sounds cheerful crossing a road in an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: A walled Roman-founded cathedral city in Cheshire, in north-west England.

clue.text: Traveller in coach, returning first class

indicators.note: returning, going back, says the combined letters are read in reverse
in places the salesman inside the vehicle

parts.note: a coach is a bus
a travelling salesman, or rep

explanation.surface: A traveller on a coach heading home in first class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion and 'returning' reverses the whole; a rep is a travelling sales representative.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means excellent, of the highest quality, top-notch.

clue.text: Old Wren turned out to be a possessive type

indicators.note: turned out suggests something shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old architect, Wren, proved to be possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has or holds property is literally the one who possesses it.

clue.text: A few lines about Greek theatre

parts.note: an ode is a short lyric poem
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A short poem on the subject of Greek drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is a British cinema chain; the name derives from the Greek odeion, a hall for music.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre or concert hall, from the ancient Greek building for musical performances.

clue.text: Short note: check it

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: An instruction to verify a brief memo.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a brief written slip, voucher or memo.

clue.text: Leave work during strike

indicators.note: during puts the work piece within the striking word

parts.note: hit means strike
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Walking off the job while workers are on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' signals the insertion. 'Hop it' is British slang for go away; OP is short for opus.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British command telling someone to clear off or go away.

clue.text: Area bound by a border, nothing out of the ordinary

indicators.note: bound by means the area letter is held inside the following words

parts.note: a verge is an edge or border

explanation.surface: An area with a border round it, nothing remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound by' puts A inside A VERGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something typical or middling is unremarkable, run-of-the-mill, standard.

clue.text: Noted boxer among finalists

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A famous boxer is one of the finalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, the world heavyweight champion, is among the most celebrated fighters.

clue.text: Heads for this outlying rocky peak

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, taken from the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Set off for this remote rocky summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads for' takes the first letters of 'this outlying rocky'. A tor is a rocky hill top, as on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a craggy hill or rocky outcrop on high moorland.

clue.text: Complete makeover incorporating new naval flag

indicators.note: incorporating means the makeover word takes in the following letter

parts.note: a redesign is a thorough overhaul

explanation.surface: A total overhaul including a new flag for the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Ensign is the British merchant navy's flag, flown by civilian vessels.
